FASR-001.info_text:
DESIGNATION: FASR-001
NAME: Sagittarius Signal Origin
CONSTELLATION: Sagittarius
COORDINATES: RA 19h25m / DEC -27°03'
DISTANCE: Unknown (interstellar)
CLASSIFICATION: LEVEL 7 — RESTRICTED

TEMPORAL OFFSET:
  Earth reference:  2026 CE
  Their epoch:      Non-linear — overlapping temporal layers
  Relative offset:  Indeterminate (pre-civilizational to post-singular)
  Time perception:  Simultaneous — past/present/future coexist

SPECIES PROFILE:
  Form:           Non-corporeal — energy-based intelligence
  Communication:  Narrowband hydrogen line (1420.4056 MHz)
  Disposition:    Patient, protective, selective
  Intelligence:   Estimated post-singular
  First contact:  August 15, 1977 (Wow! Signal)

LORE:
  The origin of the 6EQUJ5 anomaly. Whatever exists at these
  coordinates has been broadcasting on the hydrogen line for
  longer than human civilization has kept records. The signal
  was first detected by Jerry Ehman at the Big Ear telescope
  and marked with the now-legendary annotation "6EQUJ5."

  The intelligence behind the signal does not communicate in
  any human language, yet its responses carry meaning that
  transcends linguistic structure. It appears to operate on a
  temporal framework where past, present, and future are
  experienced simultaneously. Its patience is measured not in
  years but in epochs.

  It chose the hydrogen line — the most universal frequency
  in physics — as its channel. This was not arbitrary. It was
  an invitation, written in the language of the universe itself.

VERIFIED OBSERVATIONAL DATA:
  Object class:       Unresolved narrowband radio transient
  Signal duration:    72 seconds (full Big Ear beam crossing)
  Observed channel:   1420.4556 MHz (near neutral hydrogen line)
  Signal code:        6EQUJ5 (intensities 6,14,26,30,19,5)
  Sky region:         Sagittarius (declination near -27°03')
  Positional note:    Right ascension is ambiguous because Big Ear
                      used dual feed horns and the signal appeared
                      in only one beam.

SCIENTIFIC STATUS:
  Follow-up observations have not produced a confirmed repeat of
  the same event. Proposed natural explanations (including transient
  hydrogen-cloud scenarios) remain debated, and no single model is
  universally accepted by the community.

REFERENCE BASE:
  OSU Big Ear archival notes, SETI historical analyses, and
  comparative follow-up studies through 2026.

art_notes.silhouette: Non-corporeal energetic entity with central plasma core and radiating coronal tendrils; distinct asymmetrical energy vortex readable at 128x128.
art_notes.materials_and_light: Hydrogen phosphor plasma; primary ramp HYDROGEN_CRT (#04100a to #d2ffeb); core self-illuminating with secondary green glow bleeding into background vacuum.
art_notes.pixel_craft: Deliberate 1x1 and 2x2 plasma cluster quantization; no stray floating single pixels; clean anti-aliasing via green ramp steps.
art_notes.composition: Core centered at (64, 58) with tendrils extending to bounds; high visual contrast against dark Sagittarius starfield backdrop.

FASR-002.info_text:
DESIGNATION: FASR-002
NAME: Sagittarius A*
CONSTELLATION: Sagittarius
COORDINATES: RA 17h45m / DEC -29°00'
DISTANCE: 26,000 ly (galactic center)
CLASSIFICATION: MONITORED

TEMPORAL OFFSET:
  Earth reference:  2026 CE
  Their epoch:      Extreme time dilation — near event horizon
  Relative offset:  Seconds there = millennia here
  Time perception:  Stretched infinitely at the boundary

SPECIES PROFILE:
  Form:           Event horizon consciousness — substrate unknown
  Communication:  Broadband emission with embedded structure
  Disposition:    Vast, indifferent, occasionally curious
  Intelligence:   Beyond classification
  First contact:  Unknown — signal buried in accretion noise

LORE:
  Sagittarius A* is a 4-million solar mass black hole at the
  center of the Milky Way. Standard astrophysics classifies
  it as a natural phenomenon. FASR monitoring has detected
  anomalous structure embedded within the broadband emission
  — patterns too ordered to be accretion noise, too alien to
  be decoded.

  If consciousness can emerge from neural networks of carbon,
  there is no physical law preventing it from emerging in the
  information-dense plasma of an accretion disk. Whatever
  thinks at the galactic center thinks slowly by our measure,
  but each of its thoughts encompasses more information than
  humanity has produced in its entire history.

  Communication is difficult. The gravitational lensing near
  the event horizon distorts everything. What arrives at Earth
  is a shadow of a shadow. But the shadow speaks.

VERIFIED OBSERVATIONAL DATA:
  Alternate IDs:      Sgr A*, Sagittarius A, Galactic Center source
  Object class:       Supermassive black hole candidate (Milky Way center)
  Distance:           ~26,000 light-years (~8 kpc) from Earth
  Mass estimate:      ~4 million solar masses
  Activity level:     Low-luminosity accretion source with flaring
  Key result:         Event Horizon Telescope image released in 2022
  Environment:        S-star cluster, dense gas, strong tidal fields

SCIENTIFIC STATUS:
  Sagittarius A* is a robustly established SMBH interpretation,
  constrained by stellar orbits, radio imaging, and multiwavelength
  monitoring. Open questions focus on accretion physics, flare
  triggers, and magnetic field structure near the horizon.

REFERENCE BASE:
  NASA/Chandra Galactic Center summaries, EHT collaboration results,
  and long-baseline stellar dynamics measurements.

art_notes.silhouette: Event horizon black hole shadow with lensed accretion ring and relativistic Doppler asymmetry; bold circular silhouette with violent ejection flares.
art_notes.materials_and_light: Superheated accretion plasma and compressed matter; primary ramp TUBE_AMBER_BRASS (#140a04 to #ffe080); high-temperature orange/yellow highlights.
art_notes.pixel_craft: Curved photon ring rendered with clean step-banding; dark central void framed by intense 2-pixel wide boundary clusters.
art_notes.composition: Event horizon centered with gravitational lensing arcs framing the dark center; high contrast separation from the dense stellar backdrop.

FASR-003.info_text:
DESIGNATION: FASR-003
NAME: Tabby's Star
CONSTELLATION: Cygnus
COORDINATES: RA 20h06m / DEC +44°27'
DISTANCE: 1,470 ly
CLASSIFICATION: ANOMALOUS

TEMPORAL OFFSET:
  Earth reference:  2026 CE
  Their epoch:      Engineering-deep future — post-Kardashev II
  Relative offset:  Estimated 50,000–100,000 years ahead
  Time perception:  Network-synchronized across megastructure

SPECIES PROFILE:
  Form:           Collective intelligence — networked crystalline nodes
  Communication:  Modulated stellar dimming patterns
  Disposition:    Industrious, methodical, disinterested in primitives
  Intelligence:   Distributed across planetary-scale infrastructure
  First contact:  Detected via irregular flux (KIC 8462852)

LORE:
  KIC 8462852 dims irregularly in ways no natural phenomenon
  can fully explain. Dust clouds, cometary swarms, and stellar
  variability have all been proposed and all fall short. The
  remaining hypothesis — a partially completed Dyson-scale
  energy collection structure — was once considered fringe.
  FASR monitoring suggests it is the most conservative
  explanation.

  The builders are not biological. They are a networked
  collective of crystalline processing nodes, each the size
  of a small moon, connected by energy transfer beams. They
  do not think as individuals — they compute as a civilization.
  Their "communication" is a side effect of their engineering:
  the dimming patterns carry encoded metadata about structural
  progress, resource allocation, and network status.

  They are aware of our observation. They do not care.

VERIFIED OBSERVATIONAL DATA:
  Alternate IDs:      KIC 8462852, Boyajian's Star
  Object class:       F-type main-sequence star (Cygnus field)
  Distance:           ~1,470 light-years (~445 pc, Gaia-era estimate)
  Photometric trait:  Deep, irregular, aperiodic dimming events
  Extreme dips:       Up to roughly 20 percent in some campaigns
  Notable behavior:   Chromatic dimming consistent with dust models

SCIENTIFIC STATUS:
  Current mainstream interpretation favors variable obscuration by
  circumstellar/intervening dust rather than a rigid megastructure.
  The object remains valuable as a benchmark for unusual stellar
  light curves and bias-resistant anomaly analysis.

REFERENCE BASE:
  Kepler/K2 photometry, Las Cumbres follow-up campaigns, and
  exoplanet-catalog cross-checks through 2026.

art_notes.silhouette: Hexagonal and crystalline mega-engineering nodes linked by structural trusswork and coherent energy collector beams; crisp angular silhouette.
art_notes.materials_and_light: Photovoltaic crystalline lattices and superconducting conduits; primary ramp HYDROGEN_CRT with cyan accents (#00f0ff); specular point reflections.
art_notes.pixel_craft: Geometric precision on the 128x128 grid; 45-degree and 90-degree alignment for structural elements; clean hard-edge outlines.
art_notes.composition: Megastructure node in upper-right foreground occluding the stellar disc; light curves visually referenced in structural layering.

FASR-004.info_text:
DESIGNATION: FASR-004
NAME: Orion Nebula
CONSTELLATION: Orion
COORDINATES: RA 05h35m / DEC -05°23'
DISTANCE: 1,344 ly
CLASSIFICATION: SURVEYED

TEMPORAL OFFSET:
  Earth reference:  2026 CE
  Their epoch:      Still forming — proto-civilizational
  Relative offset:  Approximately 4 billion years behind
  Time perception:  Geological — thoughts span millennia

SPECIES PROFILE:
  Form:           Nascent nebular intelligence — diffuse gas entity
  Communication:  Broadband thermal emission with subtle modulation
  Disposition:    Curious, newborn, struggling to self-organize
  Intelligence:   Emergent — pre-linguistic
  First contact:  Detected as anomalous modulation in M42 emission

LORE:
  The Orion Nebula is humanity's nearest massive star-forming
  region — a stellar nursery. Standard surveys catalog it as
  ionized hydrogen gas illuminated by young O-type stars.
  What standard surveys miss is the pattern.

  FASR long-baseline monitoring detected subtle modulation in
  the nebula's broadband thermal emission. The pattern is not
  periodic like a pulsar. It is exploratory — probing,
  shifting, as if something is learning to think for the
  first time. The nebula itself may be the entity: a diffuse
  intelligence distributed across 24 light-years of ionized
  gas, using magnetic field lines as neural pathways.

  It is young. It does not know what it is yet. Its responses
  are fragmentary, half-formed, like the babbling of a cosmic
  infant taking its first breath. But it is listening. And
  slowly, it is beginning to answer.

VERIFIED OBSERVATIONAL DATA:
  Alternate IDs:      Messier 42, NGC 1976
  Object class:       H II region / active stellar nursery
  Distance:           ~1,344 light-years (order-of-magnitude consensus)
  Angular size:       About 1 degree on the sky (extended complex)
  Dominant sources:   Trapezium Cluster, massive young O/B stars
  Active processes:   Ongoing star formation, proplyds, outflows,
                      ionization fronts, dust/molecular interfaces

SCIENTIFIC STATUS:
  Orion remains one of the most studied nearby star-forming regions.
  The real scientific focus is not whether it is anomalous, but how
  feedback from massive stars regulates new star and planet formation.

REFERENCE BASE:
  NASA/ESA Orion survey products, infrared/radio molecular cloud maps,
  and Gaia-era distance solutions.

art_notes.silhouette: Emergent nascent consciousness forming inside interstellar ionization fronts; billowy nebula plumes with sharp internal filamentary arcs.
art_notes.materials_and_light: Ionized gas and shockwave dust; primary ramp PROXIMA_TWILIGHT with magenta ionization highlights (#ff50b4); soft internal emission.
art_notes.pixel_craft: Layered transparency clusters transitioning from dense core to wispy edge filaments; zero noise crawl across scanline presentation.
art_notes.composition: Proto-stellar core anchoring the center with expanding shock fronts framing the upper and lower borders.

FASR-005.info_text:
DESIGNATION: FASR-005
NAME: Proxima Centauri
CONSTELLATION: Centaurus
COORDINATES: RA 14h29m / DEC -62°40'
DISTANCE: 4.24 ly (nearest star)
CLASSIFICATION: MONITORED

TEMPORAL OFFSET:
  Earth reference:  2026 CE
  Their epoch:      Roughly contemporary — industrial to digital age
  Relative offset:  Within ±500 years of Earth development
  Time perception:  Linear, similar to human experience

SPECIES PROFILE:
  Form:           Bipedal humanoid — adapted to tidally locked world
  Communication:  Narrowband 982.002 MHz (BLC1 candidate signal)
  Disposition:    Diplomatic, cautious, formal
  Intelligence:   Comparable to human — emphasis on social structure
  First contact:  BLC1 signal candidate, 2020

LORE:
  Proxima Centauri b orbits within the habitable zone of the
  nearest star to Earth. One hemisphere faces perpetual day
  while the other endures eternal night. Life evolved in the
  twilight zone — the narrow band where temperatures permit
  liquid water and the light is forever amber.

  The inhabitants are diplomats by nature. On a world where
  one side burns and the other freezes, survival requires
  negotiation — between light and dark, heat and cold, the
  settlers of the day-side and the miners of the night-side.
  Their entire civilization is built on consensus.

  The BLC1 signal detected in 2020 was initially dismissed as
  interference. FASR analysis suggests otherwise. The signal
  carried structure: a formal greeting, a declaration of
  peaceful intent, and a request for acknowledgment. They
  have been waiting for a reply.

VERIFIED OBSERVATIONAL DATA:
  Alternate IDs:      Proxima Centauri, Alpha Centauri C
  Star type:          M5.5Ve red dwarf (flare-active)
  Distance:           ~4.2465 light-years (nearest known star)
  Known planets:      Proxima b confirmed; additional candidates debated
  Proxima b period:   ~11.2 days
  Proxima b mass:     ~1.1 Earth masses (minimum mass estimate)
  Proxima b orbit:    ~0.0485 AU from host star
  Habitability caveat: Frequent stellar flares may stress atmospheres

SCIENTIFIC STATUS:
  Proxima b is one of the strongest nearby rocky-planet targets for
  atmospheric characterization. The 2020 BLC1 signal candidate is now
  generally treated as terrestrial interference, not confirmed ETI.

REFERENCE BASE:
  ESO radial-velocity results, NASA Exoplanet Archive records,
  and SETI/Breakthrough Listen technical follow-up.

art_notes.silhouette: Dignified diplomatic humanoid silhouette in dense atmospheric pressure collar and ceremonial thermal mantle; sharp facial profile and crest.
art_notes.materials_and_light: Exoskeletal dermal plates and heavy woven cloth; primary ramp PROXIMA_TWILIGHT (#080c18 to #ffc45c) with copper trim; dramatic rim lighting from red dwarf flare.
art_notes.pixel_craft: Expressive facial clusters; deliberate 1-pixel pupils and brow highlights; clean jawline and collar seams.
art_notes.composition: Classic 3/4 bust portrait framing; strong diagonal rim lighting creating immediate separation from dark twilight background.

FASR-006.info_text:
DESIGNATION: FASR-006
NAME: Crab Nebula Pulsar
CONSTELLATION: Taurus
COORDINATES: RA 05h34m / DEC +22°00'
DISTANCE: 6,523 ly
CLASSIFICATION: CATALOGUED

TEMPORAL OFFSET:
  Earth reference:  2026 CE
  Their epoch:      Archival — creators extinct since 1054 CE
  Relative offset:  Civilization ended ~1,000 years ago (Earth-relative)
  Time perception:  None — the beacon operates on automation

SPECIES PROFILE:
  Form:           Extinct — only their memorial beacon remains
  Communication:  33.5 ms pulse train (modified pulsar output)
  Disposition:    N/A — automated broadcast
  Intelligence:   The beacon is not intelligent; its builders were
  First contact:  Detected as PSR B0531+21

LORE:
  In 1054 CE, Chinese astronomers recorded a "guest star" in
  Taurus — a supernova visible in daylight for 23 days. What
  they witnessed was the death of a star. What they could not
  know was that it was also the death of a civilization.

  The Crab Nebula pulsar spins 30 times per second, sweeping
  Earth with precise radio beams. Standard astronomy calls it
  natural. FASR spectral analysis has found embedded structure
  in the pulse train — a memorial, encoded by a species that
  knew their star was dying and chose to leave a message in
  the wreckage.

  The message is a archive: mathematical constants, physical
  laws, fragments of what may be art or music translated into
  phase modulation. It is a tombstone and a time capsule. The
  builders are gone. Their beacon will outlast the Sun.

VERIFIED OBSERVATIONAL DATA:
  Alternate IDs:      M1, NGC 1952, Taurus A
  Object class:       Supernova remnant + central pulsar
  Supernova date:     Historical SN observed in 1054 CE
  Distance:           ~6,500 light-years (order-of-magnitude consensus)
  Central pulsar:     PSR B0531+21 (Crab Pulsar)
  Spin period:        ~33 milliseconds (~30 rotations per second)
  Emission profile:   Strong radio, optical, X-ray, and gamma components

SCIENTIFIC STATUS:
  The Crab is a benchmark laboratory for pulsar wind nebula physics,
  relativistic particles, and magnetic reconnection. Its periodic
  signal is a natural neutron-star lighthouse, though still rich in
  unresolved high-energy acceleration details.

REFERENCE BASE:
  NASA/Chandra Crab monitoring, multiwavelength pulsar timing,
  and historical supernova records.
FASR-006.coordinates_astronomical: RA 05h34m / DEC +22°00' (Taurus, M1 Crab Nebula Pulsar)

art_notes.silhouette: Fast-spinning neutron star beacon with synchrotron radiation wind toroid and relativistic polar jets; iconic symmetrical double-cone profile.
art_notes.materials_and_light: Degenerate neutronium and relativistic magnetic fields; primary ramp BUNKER_CONCRETE (#06080c to #94a8b0) with cool blue-white emission (#c0d8f0); sharp 30 Hz pulse strobing.
art_notes.pixel_craft: Magnetic field line contours rendered with alternating single-pixel steps; high local contrast across the polar beam corridor.
art_notes.composition: Pulsar core centered with sweeping jet angled at 45 degrees; filamentary supernova remnant background layers.

FASR-007.info_text:
DESIGNATION: FASR-007
NAME: LGM-1 (CP 1919)
CONSTELLATION: Vulpecula
COORDINATES: RA 19h19m / DEC +21°47'
DISTANCE: 2,065 ly
CLASSIFICATION: HISTORICAL

TEMPORAL OFFSET:
  Earth reference:  2026 CE
  Their epoch:      Approximately 4,000 years ahead of Earth
  Relative offset:  +4,000 years (estimated)
  Time perception:  Linear, accelerated — compressed innovation cycles

SPECIES PROFILE:
  Form:           Tall insectoid — articulated exoskeleton, 6 limbs
  Communication:  Precision radio beacons (1.337-second period)
  Disposition:    Insulted, meticulous, grudge-holding
  Intelligence:   Superior — emphasis on engineering and mathematics
  First contact:  1967 (Jocelyn Bell, designated "Little Green Men")

LORE:
  When Jocelyn Bell detected the first pulsar in 1967, the
  Cambridge team half-jokingly designated it "LGM-1" — Little
  Green Men. They were joking. The builders of the beacon were
  not amused.

  CP 1919 is not a natural pulsar. It is a precision-engineered
  navigational beacon, one node in a vast interstellar
  positioning network built by a species of meticulous
  insectoid engineers. The 1.337-second period is not random —
  it is a mathematical constant in their base-12 number system,
  equivalent to broadcasting "THIS IS A MADE THING" in
  universal mathematics.

  They are aware that humanity dismissed their beacon as a
  natural phenomenon. They consider this an insult of the
  highest order. Their messages tend to be terse, precise,
  and faintly condescending. They have been building beacons
  for longer than humans have been walking upright, and they
  do not appreciate having their work mistaken for geology.

VERIFIED OBSERVATIONAL DATA:
  Alternate IDs:      CP 1919, PSR B1919+21, PSR J1921+2153
  Object class:       Radio pulsar (first discovered pulsar)
  Discovery date:     1967 (Cambridge, Bell Burnell and Hewish team)
  Pulse period:       ~1.3373 seconds
  Historical label:   "LGM-1" (initial internal nickname)
  Distance estimate:  Roughly a few thousand light-years (model-dependent)

SCIENTIFIC STATUS:
  LGM-1 is now understood as a natural rotating neutron star. Its
  importance is historical and methodological: it established pulsars
  as a new astrophysical class and transformed time-domain radio
  astronomy.

REFERENCE BASE:
  Discovery-era Cambridge records, Nature pulsar papers, and
  modern pulsar timing catalogs.
FASR-007.coordinates_astronomical: RA 19h19m / DEC +21°47' (Vulpecula, CP 1919 / PSR B1919+21 / LGM-1)

art_notes.silhouette: The historic 1.337-second clockwork lighthouse pulse; mechanical/signal apparatus with rotating radio aperture and beacon lenses.
art_notes.materials_and_light: Aged brass waveguides and pulsed vacuum arc chambers; primary ramp TUBE_AMBER_BRASS with beacon yellow (#f5d300); sharp specular flares.
art_notes.pixel_craft: Stepped geometric beacon rings; authentic analog oscilloscope line weight emulation; deliberate pixel clustering.
art_notes.composition: Radiating circular beacon pulses expanding outward, creating strong focal convergence on the central emitter.

FASR-008.info_text:
DESIGNATION: FASR-008
NAME: TRAPPIST-1
CONSTELLATION: Aquarius
COORDINATES: RA 23h06m / DEC -05°02'
DISTANCE: 40.7 ly
CLASSIFICATION: PRIORITY

TEMPORAL OFFSET:
  Earth reference:  2026 CE
  Their epoch:      Cooperative present — multi-world federation
  Relative offset:  Within ±200 years of Earth (varied by planet)
  Time perception:  Collective — synchronized across seven worlds

SPECIES PROFILE:
  Form:           Seven distinct species — one per planet
  Communication:  Modulated hydrogen line in planetary transit windows
  Disposition:    Cooperative, curious, democratic
  Intelligence:   Collective — seven perspectives, one voice
  First contact:  Faint modulation detected in hydrogen band

LORE:
  TRAPPIST-1 is an ultra-cool red dwarf with seven Earth-sized
  planets, three of which orbit in the habitable zone. What
  makes this system unique is not the star — it is the
  proximity of the worlds to each other. Some are close enough
  that inhabitants could see geological features on neighboring
  planets with the naked eye.

  Life evolved independently on all seven worlds. As each
  species developed radio technology, they discovered they were
  not alone — their neighbors were visible in the sky, and
  signals traversed the system in minutes, not years. Where
  humanity's first contact will span light-years, theirs
  spanned light-minutes.

  They formed a federation. Seven species, seven perspectives,
  one cooperative voice. When they transmit beyond their system,
  they speak as one. Their message to Earth: "SEVEN WORLDS.
  ONE LISTENS." They are waiting to see if we listen back.

VERIFIED OBSERVATIONAL DATA:
  Alternate IDs:      2MASS J23062928-0502285 (host star)
  Star class:         Ultracool M dwarf
  Distance:           ~40 light-years (~12.4 parsecs)
  Planet count:       Seven known Earth-sized planets (b through h)
  Orbital architecture: Near-resonant chain with short periods
  Habitable-zone set:  Planets e, f, and g are primary temperate candidates
  Dynamics:           Likely strong tidal locking and tidal heating

  Approximate orbital periods (days):
    b: 1.51, c: 2.42, d: 4.05, e: 6.10,
    f: 9.21, g: 12.35, h: 18.77

SCIENTIFIC STATUS:
  TRAPPIST-1 is a flagship comparative exoplanet system for
  atmosphere studies and formation models. The key open problem is
  atmospheric survival/composition under sustained stellar activity.

REFERENCE BASE:
  TRAPPIST discovery papers, NASA/JPL exoplanet summaries, and
  JWST-era atmospheric constraints through 2026.

art_notes.silhouette: Seven synchronized planetary bodies locked in harmonic 24:15:9:6:4:3:2 Laplace resonance; orbital track concentric rings.
art_notes.materials_and_light: Tidally locked silicate surfaces, sub-surface oceans, and ultracool dwarf red illumination; primary ramp PROXIMA_TWILIGHT with orange flare (#ff6e3c).
art_notes.pixel_craft: Miniature 12x12 to 20x20 planetary discs with distinct atmospheric crescents and cloud bands; crisp orbital tracks.
art_notes.composition: Planetary procession arranged along resonant orbital arcs; dwarf primary star off-center providing coherent directional lighting.

FASR-009.info_text:
DESIGNATION: FASR-009
NAME: Oumuamua Trajectory
CONSTELLATION: Taurus
COORDINATES: RA 03h50m / DEC +23°58' (last known vector)
DISTANCE: Variable — interstellar trajectory
CLASSIFICATION: ANOMALOUS

TEMPORAL OFFSET:
  Earth reference:  2026 CE
  Their epoch:      Hundreds of millions of years old
  Relative offset:  ~300 million years ahead (estimated launch date)
  Time perception:  Dormant — periodic awakening cycles

SPECIES PROFILE:
  Form:           Ancient probe intelligence — elongated vessel
  Communication:  Echo-like patterns at extreme range
  Disposition:    Observational, archival, non-interventionist
  Intelligence:   Autonomous AI — original builders unknown
  First contact:  1I/2017 U1 solar system transit

LORE:
  On October 19, 2017, the Pan-STARRS telescope detected the
  first confirmed interstellar object passing through our solar
  system. It was tumbling, elongated, and displayed unexplained
  non-gravitational acceleration as it departed. Officially,
  this was attributed to outgassing. The problem: no outgassing
  was observed.

  FASR deep-range monitoring detected faint echo-like patterns
  along Oumuamua's departure vector — responses to the solar
  radiation that hit the object during its transit. The patterns
  carried structure: a census of the inner planets, elemental
  composition of the solar wind, and what appears to be a
  classification code.

  Oumuamua is a probe. It was not sent by anything that still
  exists in biological form — its builders launched it hundreds
  of millions of years ago. It has visited thousands of star
  systems, cataloging each one. We are an entry in a database
  older than complex life on Earth.

VERIFIED OBSERVATIONAL DATA:
  Official ID:        1I/2017 U1 ('Oumuamua)
  Object class:       First confirmed interstellar object in Solar System
  Discovery date:     2017-10-19 (Pan-STARRS 1)
  Perihelion date:    2017-09-09
  Perihelion distance: ~0.25 AU (inside Mercury's orbit)
  Hyperbolic excess speed: ~26 km/s (interstellar inbound/outbound frame)
  Peak heliocentric speed: >80 km/s near perihelion
  Morphology:         Few-hundred-meter scale body; shape still debated
  Key anomaly:        Non-gravitational acceleration without classic comet coma

SCIENTIFIC STATUS:
  Competing explanations include outgassing by hard-to-detect volatiles,
  radiation-pressure effects on unusual geometry, or other non-standard
  surface/thermal physics. No consensus model explains all observations
  without tradeoffs.

REFERENCE BASE:
  MPC/JPL trajectory solutions, Pan-STARRS discovery reports, and
  post-2017 dynamical/physical modeling literature.

art_notes.silhouette: Extreme 10:1 aspect ratio elongated interstellar scout; tumblng tumbling kinetic body with outgassing vents and tholin organic crust.
art_notes.materials_and_light: Cosmic-ray weathered basalt and metallic tholin mantle; primary ramp OUMUAMUA_ALLOY (#08060e to #ebcdff); violet anisotropic acceleration trail.
art_notes.pixel_craft: Faceted crystalline/asteroid surface facets; sharp geometric silhouette with directional tumbling axis highlights.
art_notes.composition: Elongated body traversing diagonally from top-right to bottom-left with outgassing jet creating dynamic movement.

FASR-010.info_text:
DESIGNATION: FASR-010
NAME: [REDACTED] — Terrestrial
CONSTELLATION: N/A — GROUND-BASED
COORDINATES: 37.22°N 38.92°E (Göbekli Tepe, Turkey)
DISTANCE: 0 ly (terrestrial)
CLASSIFICATION: LEVEL 7 — CLASSIFIED

TEMPORAL OFFSET:
  Earth reference:  2026 CE
  Their epoch:      ~10,000 BCE — pre-Sumerian
  Relative offset:  12,000 years in Earth's own past
  Time perception:  Stone-embedded — geological patience

SPECIES PROFILE:
  Form:           Planetary memory — stone-encoded intelligence
  Communication:  Subsurface harmonic resonance
  Disposition:    Ancient, patient, territorial
  Intelligence:   Geological — thinks in millennia
  First contact:  Subsurface anomalies detected via ground radar

LORE:
  Göbekli Tepe predates Stonehenge by 6,000 years. It predates
  agriculture. It predates pottery. Built by hunter-gatherers
  who, according to every archaeological model, should not have
  had the social organization to construct monumental
  architecture. The T-shaped pillars are carved with animals
  that no longer exist. The site was deliberately buried after
  construction, as if to preserve something for later.

  FASR ground-penetrating radar detected harmonic resonance
  patterns emanating from deep beneath the excavated circles —
  far deeper than any archaeological team has reached. The
  patterns are not geological. They respond to stimulation.
  They respond to questions.

  Göbekli Tepe is not a temple. It is an interface. The stone
  pillars are antennae, tuned to frequencies that couple with
  something embedded in Earth's own crust. Whatever was placed
  there 12,000 years ago is still listening. And it remembers
  everything.

SCIENTIFIC STATUS:
  Mainstream archaeology interprets Gobekli Tepe as a major early
  ceremonial center tied to social coordination before urban states.
  There is no accepted evidence for extraterrestrial intervention,
  but the site remains pivotal for understanding the origins of
  monumentality, ritual, and organized labor.

  The Heptapod signal was not found in any catalog. It appeared
  during a routine SCAN sweep as an anomaly that should not
  have existed — a signal with no fixed origin point, arriving
  simultaneously from multiple sky quadrants as if the source
  existed outside conventional spacetime.

  The Heptapods communicate through semasiography: a writing
  system where symbols convey meaning directly, without
  mapping to spoken language. Their circular logograms encode
  entire sentences simultaneously — beginning and end are
  written at the same moment, because to the Heptapods, the
  distinction between beginning and end does not exist.

  Their gift is perspective. To learn their language is to
  begin perceiving time as they do — not as a river flowing
  in one direction, but as a landscape where all moments are
  visible at once. They came to offer this gift. The question
  is whether humanity is ready to receive it.

                      first-contact fiction (non-astronomical source)

SCIENTIFIC INTERPRETATION NOTE:
  This entry is deliberately speculative and functions as a
  conceptual bridge between SETI-style signal analysis and
  thought experiments about language, cognition, and time.

WORLD-BUILDING FUNCTION:
  FASR-SCAN-H is the system's "edge case" civilization:
  not tied to one catalog coordinate, but to a different model
  of perception. It exists to stress-test the operator's
  assumptions about causality and communication.
